samples.rationale: The base rate for PHEIC declarations is low, with only a few declarations typically made each year. As of May 2026, one PHEIC has been declared, suggesting heightened vigilance but not necessarily a trend of frequent declarations. Factors such as global interconnectedness and ecological changes increase the likelihood of outbreaks, but the rarity of PHEICs and improved health monitoring counterbalance this. Therefore, the probability of zero new PHEICs in the latter half of 2026 is the highest, with a lower probability for one new PHEIC and even lower for two or more.

baseline_rationale: Based on historical data, the emergence of new Public Health Emergencies of International Concern (PHEICs) can be unpredictable but tends to occur sporadically. Given the global health landscape, it is reasonable to estimate a moderate probability for no new PHEICs (0), a slightly higher chance for one new PHEIC (1), and a similar probability for two or more new PHEICs (2 or more). The probabilities reflect the uncertainty and variability in the emergence of infectious diseases.
